narrative:
The model estimated an 84.1% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt, which is why your law school application was denied. This is a high-risk prediction, not a guarantee, but it means the decision was driven mainly by concerns about your academic preparation.

The strongest factor was your class standing in your third year. A decile of 1 is far below the accepted-student average of about 5.8, and it pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year standing was the second most influential factor; a decile of 1, compared with an accepted average of 6.0, also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.30 was the third most important factor and worked in your favor: it is slightly above the accepted average of 3.23 and modestly pushed toward passing, but it did not outweigh the class-standing concerns.

Next, contact admissions to request a human review or appeal. Ask whether you can explain the reasons for your class ranks, provide evidence of improvement or extenuating circumstances, and ask what steps—such as academic advising, bar-readiness preparation, or reapplication guidance—could support reconsideration.
